scope: Inner co-op relay encoding, per-peer sequencing/ACK/control/replay, pending-byte limit, service-wide sender credit and monotonic clock lifecycle. This bounded static proof does not certify whole-module fidelity or actual networking.

wire.unknown_or_truncated: Ignored before creating peer sequence state; unused ACK/control suffix is accepted.

contracts.receive: Deliver only sequence==receive_sequence.wrapping_add(1), update receive sequence and copy payload. Duplicate/older frames are ignored; a future gap emits control(false,current receive) at most once per3s without buffering the future payload.
contracts.ack: Drain pending front records with sequence<=ACK sequence; subtract raw payload bytes and saturating-decrement sent cursor for each.
contracts.control: Drain as ACK; sent cursor=0, pending=false, control clock=None. False flag answers control(true,current receive); nonzero flag does not answer. Retained pending records replay with original IDs.
contracts.timers: Global monotonic0.5s clock publishes advanced receive sequences as ACKs; per-peer pending control retries every3s. Both compare seconds+nanos/1e9 as f32; selected transport must report state1.
contracts.secondary_reset: Actual selected-secondary replacement/re-authentication marks every relay row pending, stamps its control clock and emits control(false,current receive). Pending rows suppress outgoing game data until control reception.
contracts.sender: One service-wide f64 bucket starts full1572864 bytes, refills1572864 bytes/sec and caps at1572864. Positive credit admits one entire raw payload and may go negative; inner/outer headers consume no credit. A sent cursor tracks dispatched pending rows without removing them.
contracts.overflow: Append increments wrapping sequence and raw pending bytes before >4194304 check. Exact4MiB is admitted; overflow removes relay state and fails the corresponding guest/host connection.
contracts.constructor: Arc/Mutex aggregate stores service payload at+0x18. Initial ACK/credit clocks use constructor now; initial bucket is1572864.0.
contracts.guest_liveness: Enabled guest handle and no fatal service+1e1 overflow. On selected primary state2 or permanent-secondary failure only buffered guest messages retain liveness; otherwise active guest or buffered messages retain it.
contracts.host_peer_liveness: Selected primary state2 or permanent selected-secondary failure returns false; otherwise an existing host peer is alive while its active flag or buffered queue is nonempty.
contracts.selected_secondary_retry_getters: Vtable+40 reports actual selected-secondary presence, no permanent failure and retry clock Some; guest additionally requires enabled handle. It is distinct from remote peer wire31/32 reconnect flags at vtable+38.
contracts.peer_open_reset: Service wire24 decodes native variant4, dispatches to145bf737b and replaces/inserts the host endpoint row. Existing-host branches145bf7b54/145bf7d1b/145bf7d3b reach145bf801e; new host insertion falls through there.145bf801e initializes default inner state, then replaces/inserts that peer row before publishing the peer ID. Reset belongs to the service event, not construction of a later host connection handle.
contracts.guest_handle_lifetime: Guest handle constructor145b21850 resets Game sample caches and sends its ordinary join command; it does not reset the service-owned inner relay state. Guest close145c053b0 disables that handle, sends Leave and closes/removes the selected secondary, preserving inner peer sequence/pending state and service flags. A new guest handle in the same service wrapper retains that state.
contracts.host_handle_close: Host Close145c045b0 optionally sends Kick for an active peer, drains pending output before the selected-secondary Kick, then removes both the host endpoint row and its inner relay state. Arc+1c8 identifies the inner map at service+1b0; Arc+1e0 is its row count.
contracts.outer_command_lifetime: Wrapper145bfdf90 only locks the service, encodes the supplied outer command and submits it through the primary callback. It neither resets nor removes inner peer state; command names alone do not imply sequence teardown.

limits: REA Ghidra pseudocode is supporting evidence, not original source; merged heap/PIC tails and clock return aliases were checked against exact instructions.
Curated constructor and service projection use current exact Capstone bytes and direct caller/context, without claiming a fresh Ghidra query for those extents.
HashMap traversal order is not a recovered deterministic peer ordering guarantee.
Source connections are bound separately after implementation settles.
No compilation, compiling tests, client/game/server/network execution or original/rebuilt parity comparison was performed.
Guest handle construction/close and wire24 reset ownership are bound separately; generic Worker construction145bf61c0 is supporting context and is not a curated reconstruction contract.
